prompt: A StatefulSet named `db` asks for three replicas. What are the pods called?

choices.text: `db` followed by a template hash and a random suffix
choices.why: That is a Deployment's naming; a StatefulSet's names are fixed.
Right, and a replacement for `db-1` is called `db-1` again.

choices.text: Whatever names the template lists for them
choices.why: A template describes one pod; the ordinal numbers are added by the controller.

choices.text: The names of the nodes they run on
choices.why: Two of them ran on the same node; names come from the StatefulSet.

prompt: `db-0` started at 16:49:56, `db-1` four seconds later, `db-2` five seconds after that. Why not all at once?
hint: What does a database cluster need from its first member?

choices.text: The scheduler places one pod per second
choices.why: The scheduler placed three Deployment pods in one second in lesson 8.

choices.text: Each pod waited for its disk to be formatted
choices.why: Disks were provisioned, but the order comes from the StatefulSet itself.

choices.text: The StatefulSet waits for each pod to be ready before starting the next one
choices.why: Right. Ordered start is the default, because later members often join the first one.

choices.text: Busybox images start slowly
choices.why: They start in well under a second; the wait is deliberate.

hint: The first label of the name is a pod.

choices.text: The three pods' addresses
choices.why: That is what the Service's own name returned.

choices.text: The address of `db-1` alone
choices.why: Right: a headless Service gives each pod a name of its own.

choices.text: The Service's ClusterIP
choices.why: A headless Service has none; `clusterIP: None`.

choices.text: An error, because pods have no DNS names
choices.why: Pods behind a headless Service do; it answered with one address.

prompt: After `db-1` was deleted and came back, what did `cat /data/born /data/last-order` print, and why?
hint: Which object did the data live in?

choices.text: Nothing: a new pod starts with an empty disk
choices.why: The new pod was given the old pod's claim, `data-db-1`.

choices.text: Only `db-1`; the order was in the deleted pod's memory
choices.why: `order-1042` was written to a file on the disk, and it was printed.

choices.text: `db-0` and `order-1042`, from the first pod's disk
choices.why: Each pod has its own claim; `db-1` never sees `db-0`'s.

choices.text: `db-1` and `order-1042`: the disk is bound to the name
choices.why: Right. The claim `data-db-1` outlived the pod and went to its replacement.

prompt: Ana scaled `db` from three replicas to one. Which claims were left afterwards?
hint: A disk is the one thing that cannot be recreated from a file.

choices.text: Only `data-db-0`
choices.why: All three were listed afterwards, still `Bound`.

choices.text: All three
choices.why: Right. Scaling down keeps the disks, so scaling up again finds them.

choices.text: `data-db-0` and `data-db-1`, because `db-2` was deleted first
choices.why: `db-2` went first, but its claim stayed with the other two.

choices.text: None: the volumes are deleted with the StatefulSet's pods
choices.why: Deleting them is left to somebody, on purpose.

prompt: Why did the replacement `db-1` come back on `shop-worker2`, the node it had been on?
hint: Where does a local-path disk live?

choices.text: StatefulSets always keep a pod on its first node
choices.why: With network storage the pod could move; here the disk decided.

choices.text: The scheduler picked it at random
choices.why: It had no choice: only one node holds that directory.

choices.text: Its disk is a directory on that node
choices.why: Right. The pod has to go where its disk is; lesson 26 shows how the volume says so.

choices.text: The headless Service only resolves names on that node
choices.why: DNS answers from any pod in the cluster, as the probe on another node showed.

hint: It has no single address at its top.
